title: Paperclip scientists in New Mexico mail Soviet-held colleagues

tellings.quote: >> Because the the the Russian scientists they had in New Mexico, >> right, were going into the village into the local towns and they were sending mail >> back to Germany which would then get sent over by Courier to the Russian scientists in the Soviet Union.

plain: In the late 1940s, scientists brought to New Mexico under Operation Paperclip, the American programme that recruited German scientists after the Second World War, went into nearby towns and mailed letters to Germany, which were then carried by courier to colleagues held in the Soviet Union. A researcher and author named Peter Levenda tells Michels this without naming a source. If true, it would mean American secrets had a quiet path straight to the Soviets.
